chapter: Louisville, Buck and the carnival years
title: Getting Buck out of school; Bubbles as a born leader
summary: He needs Buck's mother to sign papers; he describes himself as born a leader and sets off to see Buck's principal.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So I gotta get Buck out of school.

I've got to get Buck -- what are you saying. Do you remember what you said? The man is going to take us to New York, that's what I told you, that's the last thing I said to you, he's going to take us to New York and he said get your mother to sign the papers and so and so, I'll take you to New York. How did it go so fast, that's what you said. Now I'm back into where I left off at by saying to you I had to get Buck out of school. Now, 'cause I've got to get Buck's mother to sign the paper to get him out of school, to take him to New York. Go ahead, you want to ask something?
You just seemed like a self-assured kind of kid. You pretty much knew what
you wanted right from the start. You were a leader.

Born that way I guess. Born like that, man. Been that way since I was born. Only thing I didn't know is the difference between a man and his wife. Didn't know that difference. I didn't know that difference. That's the only thing that slowed me down. So the good Lord took my father because I didn't know that difference. If I did know that difference he wouldn't have taken my father when he did. Okay?
I don't know exactly what you mean.
Oh, God, tell you that later. I want to get to this point where I just said I got to get Buck out of school. So I go to Buck's school to see his principal.
